title: Day 3: The digestive system
sub: Day 3 (Fri). The organs in order, what each one does, and why the small intestine is so good at absorbing food. About 25 minutes.
skill: The Because Chain: cause → effect → consequence.
target: For the small intestine, always link the feature to what it does: villi → big surface area → absorbs food faster.

sections.sub: Digestion breaks big molecules in food into small molecules of nutrients, small enough to pass into the blood.

blocks.q: Tap the parts in the order food passes through them.
blocks.done: Mouth → gullet → stomach → small intestine → large intestine → rectum → anus.

o: Food is chewed by the teeth and mixed with saliva
blocks.why: Teeth break food into smaller pieces, and saliva starts to soften and digest it.

o: Food is mixed with digestive juices and acid
blocks.why: The stomach churns the food with acid and digestive juices.

blocks.q: What happens in the small intestine?
o: Juices from the liver and pancreas finish digestion, and small nutrient molecules pass into the blood
blocks.why: Digestion is completed here, and the small molecules are absorbed through the wall into the bloodstream.

blocks.q: What happens in the large intestine?
o: Water is absorbed back into the body, leaving solid waste (faeces)
blocks.why: Only food that could not be digested gets this far. Water is taken back into the body.

o: The anus stores faeces; the rectum lets them out
The rectum stores faeces; the anus is a ring of muscle that lets them out
blocks.why: Rectum = store. Anus = the muscular ring the faeces leave through.

sections.sub: Why the small intestine is adapted (suited) to its job.

blocks.html:
The small intestine’s job: absorb small food molecules into the blood quickly, before the undigested food moves on.
How it is adapted:
  • a thin wall, so molecules only have a short way to go;
  • it is covered in tiny finger-like villi, which give it a huge surface area;
  • the villi contain blood capillaries that carry the absorbed food away.
Moving food along: muscles in the wall of the gut squeeze food along, like squeezing toothpaste. Fibre is not digested, but gives the muscles something to push against, so a high-fibre diet helps prevent constipation.

o: They give the small intestine a big surface area, so food is absorbed faster
blocks.why: More surface area = more space for molecules to pass into the blood at once.

blocks.q: Why is it useful that the wall of the small intestine is thin?
o: Food molecules have only a short distance to travel into the blood
blocks.why: A short distance means the molecules get into the blood quickly.

blocks.q: Fibre is not digested. Why is it still good for you?
o: It gives you lots of energy
It adds bulk, so the gut muscles can push food along, which helps prevent constipation
It is absorbed by the villi
blocks.why: Fibre adds bulk for the muscles to push against.

blocks.q: Why does the small intestine absorb food so quickly? Tap the links in order.
items: The small intestine is covered in villi.
The villi give it a very big surface area.
So more food molecules can pass through the wall at the same time.
So food is absorbed into the blood quickly.
blocks.done: Feature → big surface area → more molecules at once → fast absorption.

blocks.q: Describe the adaptations of the small intestine and explain how each one helps it absorb food.

points.t: villi give a big surface area, so more food is absorbed at once
a thin wall, so molecules have a short distance to travel
blood capillaries in the villi carry the food away

starters: The small intestine is covered in villi, which…

blocks.q: Describe what happens to a piece of bread from when you eat it to when the waste leaves your body.

points.t: mouth: chewed by teeth and mixed with saliva
gullet: passes down to the stomach
stomach: mixed with acid and digestive juices
small intestine: digestion finished (juices from liver and pancreas); small molecules absorbed into the blood
large intestine: water absorbed back into the body, leaving faeces
rectum stores faeces; they leave through the anus

mark.note: This is a 6-mark “describe in detail”: one mark per stage, in the right order. Name each organ and say what happens there.

items: I can list the organs in order from mouth to anus.
I can say what each organ does in one sentence.
I can explain villi → surface area → faster absorption.
I can explain why fibre matters.

blocks.q: “Why is your small intestine covered in tiny villi?”
blocks.note: For the parent: listen for big surface area → more food absorbed at once → faster. “To absorb food” alone is only half: ask “how do the villi help?”
